reasons: R18, R01, F13: receivables growing much faster than sales (>10 pts) with elevated DSO, and a single customer holding 10-25% of receivables, is a classic signal of aggressive or premature revenue recognition or collectibility problems.
R08, R19: high positive total accruals and operating cash flow well below net income (<0.8x) indicate earnings not backed by cash, a key accrual-based misstatement indicator.
R09: Beneish M-score above the -1.78 threshold flags elevated manipulation likelihood, driven by the DSRI, AQI and depreciation components (R01, R03, R05).
R05, F25: depreciation slowing sharply alongside a voluntary accounting change suggests possible earnings management through useful-life or method changes.
R03, R13: high asset quality index and soft assets above 75% of total assets mean more capitalised costs and judgement-heavy balances that are easier to manipulate.
F14, R15: a CEO or CFO change during the year coinciding with rising ROA adds some management-transition risk.

F01, F03, F07, F16, F17, F18, F24: mitigants include no material weakness, an unqualified ICFR opinion, no prior-period correction, no SEC, class action or other government investigation, and no critical audit matter topics flagged.

R17, R07, R16, F19, F21, F20: Dechow F-score below threshold, stable or falling leverage, no securities issued, no covenant issues, no capital raise and no revenue/EPS-linked incentive pay reduce pressure and financing-related motives, so the score stays moderate.
